summary: Turned the last open half of the trim child's gap from a source reading into an executed observation and queued that execution. The harness gains one case, memory_storage_below_trimmed_request, which drives the shipped in-memory storage directly through the public Storage trait instead of through the protocol: it appends four entries, emits STORPROBE_BASE with the log length, trims two entries, then calls get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) below the trimmed index each inside its own catch_unwind, calls get_suffix(2) at the trimmed index itself, and reports the log length, both panic flags and the state and length of the read at the trimmed index. That makes the question the gap asks - below a compacted index, panic or silently empty suffix - answerable by observation for this implementation and build profile, rather than only by the unguarded subtractions in memory_storage.rs that the newly recorded knowledge entry describes; the second comparison keeps the probe honest by requiring the read at the trimmed index itself to succeed, so a total failure of the storage is not read as the below-trimmed behaviour. The experiment is filed as a successor of the trim child's own experiment, so its receipt lands in the investigation whose gap it answers, with the same investigation, scope, prefix and semantic-change record as the rest of the lineage; no other record changed this turn. Incomplete by design: the receipt is not yet read, so the storage-level half of the gap remains marked unresolved until the observation arrives, and the forwarded-compaction peer sampling and the delivery of a Snapshot compaction to a NoSnapshot instance still need their own cases.
